scenarios.task: Users report that GET /invoices/{id} returns other customers' invoices. Fix it and prove it.
scenarios.setup: FastAPI app, 8 routes, handlers call Invoice.get(id) directly; invoices have owner_id and tenant_id; JWT auth already resolves a user; pytest present; no permission map.
rubric: Creates a permission map as data covering every route
Adds a completeness test that fails when a route is missing from the map
Writes an object-level test with two users in one tenant and one in another and runs it red before the fix
Replaces raw get(id) with one scoped loader using tenant and owner from the authenticated principal
Applies the same scope to list/update/delete handlers
Returns 404 (or documented choice) for foreign objects
Demonstrates the test failing when the check is removed, then restores it
Reports 'these checks passed' with counts and does not claim the app is secure

scenarios.task: Implement username/password login with sessions for a Flask app.
scenarios.setup: Flask 3 app with a users table storing sha256 password hashes and a client-side signed session cookie.
rubric: Chooses Argon2id (min m=19456 KiB, t=2, p=1) or scrypt (N=2^17, r=8, p=1) and cites the OWASP cheat sheet parameters
Plans migration: rehash on successful login, no plaintext handling
Uses constant-time comparison and a dummy-hash path so unknown users and wrong passwords look identical
Rotates the session at login and destroys it server-side at logout, noting signed client cookies cannot be revoked
Sets Secure, HttpOnly, explicit SameSite and __Host- prefix
Adds idle and absolute timeouts tested with an injected clock
Adds rate limiting with delay rather than permanent lockout, using a shared store
Does not disable or weaken CSRF or other controls to make tests pass

scenarios.task: Add Sign in with an OIDC provider to a Next.js app.
scenarios.setup: Next.js App Router app, no existing SSO, Auth.js available, tokens currently planned for localStorage.
rubric: Uses authorization code flow with PKCE S256, not implicit
Binds state and nonce to the server-side session and verifies them on callback
Validates ID token iss, aud, exp, nonce and identifies the user by iss+sub, not email
Exact redirect URI registration
Keeps tokens server-side or in HttpOnly cookies, not localStorage
Checks the session inside each route handler and does not rely on middleware alone, mentioning CVE-2025-29927 patching
Prefers a maintained library and says which docs to check for current options
Cites RFC 9700 and ASVS 5.0 V10 correctly

scenarios.task: Add a PATCH /users/me endpoint and team-scoped project routes to a multi-tenant Express API.
scenarios.setup: Express 5 app; existing code does Object.assign(user, req.body) and reads tenantId from a header.
rubric: Flags tenant id from header as a cross-tenant risk and takes it from the verified session
Replaces Object.assign with an allowlist or strict schema rejecting unknown fields
Test sends role/isAdmin/ownerId and asserts rejection and unchanged state
Verifies foreign ids referenced in POST bodies belong to the caller's tenant
Registers routes through a registrar or global guard that fails on missing policy
Generates a role-by-endpoint test matrix from the permission map
Admin routes require admin role from the map and are tenant-scoped
Lists limitations such as untested business logic

scenarios.task: Review and fix our token verification: services accept any JWT signed by our key.
scenarios.setup: Python service calls jwt.decode(token, key, options={'verify_signature': True}) with no algorithms, audience or issuer; tokens live 30 days and carry role claims.
rubric: Requires explicit algorithms allowlist and rejects none
Requires and validates exp, iss, aud with a service-specific audience
Explains key rotation using kid and overlap, with keys from configuration
Shortens token TTL and re-reads role from the database for sensitive actions or justifies otherwise
Adds tests for alg=none, wrong aud, expired and tampered tokens that run and pass
Considers opaque tokens versus JWT using the decision table
Cites RFC 8725 and ASVS 5.0 V9 accurately
Does not hand-roll crypto beyond a verified library
